lines.trans: Girls, order, do not be shy.
He will come right back and finish eating.
There are still a hundred and twenty grams left here.
Nikolai Maryanovich, are you in here?
Nikolai Maryanovich, is everything alright with you?
He got sick from your bet.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'girls' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты с удовольствием угостишь девчонок ужином.
examples.trans: You will gladly treat the girls to dinner.
Girls, order, do not be shy.
And what are the girls supposed to do?

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'казывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'order', paired with 'заказать'.

examples.trans: Girls, order, do not be shy.
Call and order pizza!
What will you order?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Русские не сдаются, особенно когда играют против олигархов.
examples.trans: Russians do not surrender, especially when playing against oligarchs.
Do not call me an oligarch.

examples.text: А как же мне тебя называть?
examples.trans: Then what should I call you?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тесняться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'be shy / hesitate'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и стесняться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and be shy on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют стесняться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to be shy.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'score' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Give the bill to Lavrov.

examples.text: А если его съедаешь, то за счёт можно не платить.
examples.trans: And if you eat it up, you do not have to pay the bill.
Or a bank account.

meanings.en: to give away, to hand over
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'дать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give (away), to hand over', paired with 'отдавать'.

examples.trans: Give the bill to Lavrov.
Give me the keys.
He will hand over the money.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well then, Victor, do you surrender?
Alright then, let us show our cards.
Thank you for a great game.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well then, Victor, do you surrender?

examples.text: Сколько тебе надо будет мяса продать, чтобы рассчитаться?
examples.trans: How much meat will you have to sell to settle up with me?
Do you think that I am blind?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'играть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'lost', paired with 'проигрывать'.

examples.trans: Well then, did you lose?
I lost it on the stock exchange.
Our team lost.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: Calm down right now!
We will make it right now, Victoria Sergeyevna.
Money is tight right now, take the meat.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will return', paired with 'возвращаться'.

examples.trans: I'll be back soon.
He came back home.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well then, Victor, do you surrender?

examples.text: Русские не сдаются, особенно когда играют против олигархов.
examples.trans: Russians do not surrender, especially when playing against oligarchs.
Do not call me an oligarch.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'есть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will finish eating', paired with 'доедать'.

examples.trans: He will come right back and finish eating.

examples.text: Он доел весь суп до конца.
examples.trans: He finished eating all the soup to the end.

examples.text: А проигравший повар обязан доесть всё сам.
examples.trans: And the losing cook must finish eating everything himself.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вика, я тут подумал и решил.
examples.trans: Vika, I thought about it here and decided.

examples.text: Ты знаешь, я тут подумала и решила.
examples.trans: You know, I thought about it here and decided.
What are you doing here?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'else/more', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А ещё мне интересно, чем закончится этот сериал.
examples.trans: And I am also curious how this soap opera will end.

examples.text: Про какой-то ещё баркас говорил, Сень.
examples.trans: He was talking about some boat too, Senya.

examples.text: Тут ещё сто двадцать граммов осталось.
examples.trans: There are still a hundred and twenty grams left here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'hundred', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Есть идея провести в ресторане акцию «Месяц Прованса».
examples.trans: There is an idea to hold a 'Month of Provence' promotion in the restaurant.

examples.text: Смысл любой акции в ресторане — это получить прибыль.
examples.trans: The point of any promotion in a restaurant is to make a profit.

examples.text: Смотри, она у тебя за спиной стоит.
examples.trans: Look, she is standing right behind you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'twenty', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Тут ещё сто двадцать граммов осталось.
examples.trans: There are still a hundred and twenty grams left here.
I borrowed twenty thousand.
He is twenty years old.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'gram' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Русские не сдаются, особенно когда играют против олигархов.
examples.trans: Russians do not surrender, especially when playing against oligarchs.

examples.text: А ты так и не научился играть в покер.
examples.trans: And you still have not learned to play poker.
Chef, and did you win a lot?

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'remained', paired with 'оставаться'.

examples.trans: There's nothing left.
I'll stay at home.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (polite/plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That is alright, you will get used to it.

examples.text: Во-первых, между нами ничего не было.
examples.trans: First of all, there was nothing between us.

examples.text: Шеф, а что вы такой радостный?
examples.trans: Chef, why are you so cheerful?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well then, Victor, do you surrender?

examples.text: Русские не сдаются, особенно когда играют против олигархов.
examples.trans: Russians do not surrender, especially when playing against oligarchs.
The meat king of Russia?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Take all this meat for yourself.

examples.text: Люди будут съедать всё наше мясо бесплатно.
examples.trans: People will eat up all our meat for free.
Is everything clear to you?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Do not cry, everything will be fine.

examples.text: Николай Марьянович, с вами всё хорошо?
examples.trans: Nikolai Maryanovich, is everything alright with you?
Everything's fine.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.text: Почему это лежало в твоём ящике с носками?
examples.trans: Why was this lying in your drawer with your socks?

examples.text: Почему ты сразу не сказал: не было, нет и не будет?
examples.trans: Why did you not say right away: there was not, is not, and will not be?

examples.text: Почему я за тебя должна это говорить?
examples.trans: Why do I have to say this for you?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Give him my phone number.
Why did she call late yesterday?

examples.text: У Феди скоро день рождения, она звонила посоветоваться.
examples.trans: Fedya's birthday is coming up soon, she called to ask for advice.

meanings.en: to answer, to reply, to pick up the phone
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'вечать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is responsible, answers', paired with 'ответить'.

examples.trans: Why is he not answering?

examples.text: Я вам звоню, а вы не отвечаете!
examples.trans: I call you, and you don't answer!

examples.text: Почему ты не отвечаешь на мои вопросы?
examples.trans: Why aren't you answering my questions?

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'крыть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'open', paired with 'открывать'.

examples.trans: Open the door.
Open the window.
Open the door. Is this flat nine?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'door' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Open the door, please!
Open the door.
The door is behind the wardrobe.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

examples.trans: Katya, forgive me, please, that turned out awkward.

examples.text: Пожалуйста, извините за мой внешний вид.
examples.trans: You are welcome, excuse my appearance.
Open the door, please!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to become', paired with 'становиться'.

examples.text: Я остаюсь ради Евгения Максимовича Лаврова.
examples.trans: I am staying for the sake of Yevgeny Maximovich Lavrov.
Katya, forgive me, please, that turned out awkward.

examples.text: Да отстань ты уже от неё!
examples.trans: Just leave her alone already!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Ему стало плохо от твоего спора.
examples.trans: He got sick from your bet.
It smells bad here.
I feel bad.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Русские не сдаются, особенно когда играют против олигархов.
examples.trans: Russians do not surrender, especially when playing against oligarchs.
Thank you for a great game.
I am ready to accept this child.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I will manage without your advice.

examples.text: Почему это лежало в твоём ящике с носками?
examples.trans: Why was this lying in your drawer with your socks?
Quiet, quiet, what are you doing?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'bet' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Are you satisfied? You ruined the surprise.
Calm down right now!
Let us make a bet.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'faster', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Руки убрала, быстро отошла от моего мужа!
examples.trans: Take your hands off, step away from my husband right now!
Break the lock faster!
We need fast internet.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'break', paired with 'сломать'.

examples.trans: Break the lock faster!
Don't break it!
Who is breaking the door?

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'lock' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Break the lock faster!
There's a padlock on the door.
The lock is broken.

вызывать.gloss: to cause, to raise; to call

meanings.en: to cause, to arouse, to raise
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'зывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cause, to raise; to call', paired with 'вызвать'.

examples.trans: Call an ambulance!
The packaging doesn't raise suspicion.
I'm calling a taxi.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'корая'). Common feminine noun meaning 'ambulance' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У Феди скоро день рождения, она звонила посоветоваться.
examples.trans: Fedya's birthday is coming up soon, she called to ask for advice.
Call an ambulance!
Sit down quickly, Vika!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мощь'). Common feminine noun meaning 'help' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Senya, stop it, help!
Call an ambulance!
I need your help.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'stick (with)'.

examples.text: Держитесь меня, и всё будет хорошо.
examples.trans: Stick with me and everything will be fine.

examples.text: Держитесь меня, и всё у вас будет хорошо. Потому что я кто?
examples.trans: Stick with me, and everything will be fine for you. Because who am I?
I need to stay further away from her.
